prompts.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: single photorealistic rehabilitation movement demonstration, action 146 T-AXU-049, step s01.
Input images: all three input images are identity/clothing/photography/background reference images only, NOT pose targets.
Create one coherent full-body studio photo of the SAME adult East Asian woman shown in the three reference photos: matching face, age, skin tone, body proportions, black ponytail, plain white short-sleeve T-shirt and dark gray full-length trousers. Soft gray-blue seamless studio backdrop and floor, soft diffused studio light, realistic mild contact shadows.
Pose: stable half-kneeling, HER LEFT knee resting on a small rectangular soft foam knee pad and HER RIGHT foot planted flat on the floor forward, both at separate clear support positions. Left lower leg extends behind her with natural relaxed foot; right knee bent roughly a right angle. Torso and pelvis upright and neutral, no lean, no twist. Both elbows bent, hands lightly together in front of the center of the chest, relaxed natural fingers. Head upright, calm neutral expression, gazing along her body's forward direction.
A single fixed handrail is to her side within comfortable reach, without blocking her body. It is an appropriately sized horizontal grab bar fixed to two floor-mounted vertical posts, with mounting bases firmly anchored on the floor. Both anchor bases and complete knee pad visible. She is not holding the handrail in this frame, both hands remain at her chest.
Camera: fixed three-quarter front oblique view, about 35 degrees off her forward direction, at torso level, horizontal lens, natural perspective. Full head, both hands, full legs and both bare feet, right foot-floor support and left knee-pad support ALL fully inside the frame with margins. Clear separation of foreground right leg and rear left knee. Use a square image with ample space for the full kneeling subject, pad and handrail; no excessive wide-angle distortion.
Constraints: one woman, one still pose, natural anatomy and accurate left/right sides. Hands must not reach floor. No kettlebell or other weights, no therapy bands, no chair, no extra equipment. No words, labels, numbering, arrows, lines, logos or watermarks, no collage, no duplicated limb or person. Preserve the reference appearance faithfully.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: rehabilitation demonstration 146 T-AXU-049 s01, revision to make correct left/right half-kneeling support unambiguous.
Input image: edit target, preserve exactly the same woman, facial identity, black ponytail, white short-sleeve shirt, dark gray trousers, bare feet, blue knee pad, stainless-steel rail and gray-blue studio photo style.
Change the staging and camera into a clear THREE-QUARTER FRONT view: camera only 25 degrees to the woman's anatomical RIGHT of her straight-ahead line (closer to frontal than the current side view).
Critical anatomical pose: HER RIGHT LEG is the FORWARD leg, so her right bent knee and her right flat bare foot must appear at the LEFT FOREGROUND side of the image. HER LEFT KNEE is the REAR kneeling support, resting on the soft blue pad at the RIGHT REAR side of the image; her left lower leg and bare foot extend naturally behind from that knee. This is a half-kneel, not two knees or standing. Show separate complete foreground right foot and rear left knee-pad support. Right knee roughly 90 degrees, front foot aligned forward and flat. Torso and pelvis upright and facing straight ahead with NO twist. Both hands lightly together at the center of the chest; elbows bent; head upright.
Keep the stainless rail off to her side, comfortably reachable, with BOTH floor-mounted support posts and both bolted anchor plates completely visible. Do not let the rail obscure either leg support. Frame the entire head, both hands, full legs and both feet with comfortable margins. Square full-body image, stable horizontal camera, realistic proportions, soft studio lighting.
No text, labels, numbers, arrows, logos, watermark, collage, extra people, duplicated limbs, weights or other equipment. One single still pose.
